correctness.rationale: For finite \(d\)-regular bipartite \(H\) without four-cycles, any mixed independent set in the cross-edge complement \(G\) has a singleton on one side; maximality gives exactly the centered stars of \(H\). Conditional on the earliest two feasible vertices, the second is opposite with probability \(d/(n+d-1)\); alternatively \(d(d-1)\) same-side second choices retain a unique common missing neighbor, which wins the residual race with probability \(1/(n-d+1)\). This proves \(p_{n,d}=dn/((n+d-1)(n-d+1))\); three disjoint early-order scenarios prove all individual atom masses, with a separate \(d=1\) pair argument. Degree-square counting gives \(n\ge1+d(d-1)\), yielding uniform asymptotics and prime-power projective-plane sharpness. Independent exact-rational dynamic programming compared full output atoms and moments on matching deletions, one/multiple missing cycles and the Fano incidence graph; a direct enumeration of \(8!\) permutations and a four-cycle counterexample passed 441 exact checks. Finite checks alone are not proof.

The published scientific literature and relevant mathematical claims were compared at the level of implication, rather than title similarity. The absence of a matching search result does not constitute a general uniqueness proof; listed risks remain.

value.rationale: Random-order greedy MIS is an established stochastic adsorption/algorithmic observable. Sparse four-cycle-free edge deletions from a dense balanced biclique generate qualitatively different successful full-class and rare small-star outcomes. The theorem identifies every output atom uniformly over all eligible incidence structures, quantifies the probability of catastrophic small outputs, and gives the sharp worst-case \(n^{3/2}\) variance order realized by projective-plane designs. These are motivated family-wide stochastic structural and risk statements rather than a one-off table entry or renaming.
